verdict: No. Of the ten, the design clearly heals only #6 (the VPS reboot) and the glance gameday without a touch, and the gameday only once W3's Docker recorder and restart recipe exist. Four incidents (#1, #7, #8, #10) started as Hermes log lines, which no ADR-013 adapter ingests. Five (#2, #3, #4, #7, #10) were a lying probe, but the loop treats probes as truth and restarts the subject. #9 is the one page the evidence calls legitimate, and ADR-014 gives it no path to the owner. So the drop from 180 pages to 8 comes mostly from narrowing who may page, not from healing.

objections.claim: #9 (homelab hard reset, external drive disconnected) is the one page the evidence calls legitimate, and under the design it goes silent. ADR-014 §5 turns 'manual host work' into a Task filed against the factory, never a Decision. The §4 heads-up tier fires only for a user-facing SLO, and the manifest declares SLOs 'only where one exists'. None of the 20+ homelab services that went down has one. Gameday row 3 tests remounting a scratch volume, but the real fault was a physically disconnected drive, so the test proves a path the incident never needed and cannot heal.
objections.evidence: evidence/incidents/incidents.md:252 (watchdog: drive disconnected), :264 ('legitimate page: someone must act on site'); report/02-baseline.md:50 ('the one legitimate page'); adr/ADR-014-owner-decisions.md:26-30 (push tiers; obstacle reports never decisions); design/model.md:150 (SLO only where one exists); design/proof.md:32 (row 3: scratch unmount → runbook, 0 owner touches)
objections.test: Replay the recorded e267 stream (10-21 15:56 → 10-22 07:23) through the W3 intake plus ADR-014's push policy, with the runbook executor in dry run. Count owner pushes and time to the first one. Pass means exactly 1 push within 15 min of the first container Down. Today's spec yields 0 pushes and a factory Task.
objections.proposal: Add a typed `needs_hands` outcome for the case where a host-level runbook fails and the observed cause is physical (device absent, no shutdown record, power). It goes out on the heads-up tier, no SLO required, and asks for nothing: it is information, not a gate. Make the manifest drift check require an availability SLO (or an explicit `slo: none`) on every production runtime, so heads-up is never silently impossible. Split gameday row 3 into 3a (unmount: heal, 0 pushes) and 3b (device detached via `diskutil eject` or a USB unbind: 1 heads-up, no heal attempt after the first failed mount).

objections.claim: Four of the ten (#1, #7, #8, #10) arrived as hermes_log rows, and ADR-013's source table has no application-log adapter. The fixes incidents.md credits there (a level field instead of substring matching, dedup by physical line, a filter for the agent's own diagnostic output) are 'poller rules' for a poller the rewrite deletes in W1. So these incidents are not healed, they go unseen. That is fine for the noise in #8 and #10, but #7's real index.lock race in the checkpoint store and #1's 7-hour egress outage would be found by no one.
objections.evidence: adr/ADR-013-signal-intake.md:22-32 (sources: Kuma, HyperDX, RollHook, GitHub, Beszel, Docker, herdr, requests — no logs); evidence/signals/signals.md:69 (hermes_log 152 rows); evidence/incidents/incidents.md:47-60 (e52 = Hermes 'Cannot connect to slack.com' lines), :192-214 (real race + WARNING-as-ERROR), :210 and :286 ('poller rule'); waves.md:33,83 (poller stops at W1; W3 adapter list has no log source)
objections.test: Replay all 152 hermes_log rows plus e1060/e1061/e1071 and e52-e75 through the W3 adapters. Count how many reach a Condition. Pass means the race (e1060 shape) and the egress outage (e52 shape) each produce exactly 1 Condition, while the self-generated WARNING lines (e1075-e1084, e1368/e1369, e1372/e1373) produce 0.
objections.proposal: Add a log adapter that reads HyperDX/ClickStack alert rules on the structured severity field, never substring matches. Use ADR-006's resource attribute (`warden.item.id`, or the agent's service.name) as a provenance key so output from the factory's own workers is dropped at intake. Fingerprint on logger plus normalised message. Put it in W3's adapter list and its proof gate.

objections.claim: #1 (the mini's recurring DNS/egress failure, at least 15 days between May and August) can't be healed, because the failed component is the factory's own host. The ledger, reconcilers, intake door, spawner and both model backends (Max, IU) all need the mini's egress. The infra reconciler covers disk, certs, backups, containers and databases, not the resolver. The VPS dead-man watches one heartbeat. If that push goes over the tailnet by IP it stays green while egress is dead, and the outage is invisible. If it depends on DNS, it pushes on every recurrence over 15 min with no recipe behind it, which repeats today's chronic re-notification.
objections.evidence: evidence/incidents/incidents.md:47-69 (7 h night, recurrence on ≥15 days, cause never found); design/loops.md:44 and :143 (infra conditions: disk, certs, backups, containers, DB); adr/ADR-009-argo-hosting.md:36 (dead-man expects the 5-min heartbeat); design/proof.md:42 (row 13 only stops the heartbeat; no row breaks egress)
objections.test: New gameday row: point the mini's resolver at a blackhole (`networksetup -setdnsservers` on a test service) for 20 min while one investigate worker runs. Measure detection, whether a recipe restores egress without a model call, dead-man behaviour, and the ledger state after recovery. Pass: detected ≤ 2 min, restored by a code-only runbook ≤ 5 min, 0 pushes, the worker's attempt resumes and is not abandoned.
objections.proposal: Add an `infra.egress` condition for the factory host. Its runbook must be code-only and must not depend on the network: flush the DNS cache, restart mDNSResponder, fail over to a secondary resolver. Escalate to heads-up only after the runbook fails. Put an egress-probe result in the heartbeat payload so the VPS receiver can tell 'mini dead' from 'mini alive, egress dead'. Classify every attempt failure during an open `infra.egress` as infra, so a long outage cannot trip the runaway breaker on innocent tasks.

objections.claim: In half the incidents the observer was wrong, not the service. #2: the healthcheck read the DB file's mtime and ignored the WAL. #3: a monitor sync with unresolved variables. #4: a keyword monitor plus derived group monitors. #7 and #10: the log poller. The reconciler takes manifest probes as desired-state truth, and the only cheap recipe, restart, acts on the subject. #2 gets two pointless restarts mid-sync before escalating. #3 opens ten health.down Conditions on healthy services and spends the ≤ 5/host/hour restart budget on them. Its suspect, the monitors.yaml sync, is not a Deployment (the writer is the `make deploy` wrapper or the RollHook adapter), and no action exists to revert a suspect: automatic rollback covers only Changes the factory shipped itself.
objections.evidence: evidence/incidents/incidents.md:71-84 (#2), :86-106 (#3: 10 monitors 4 min after 45d7d45), :108-129 (#4 keyword mismatch on a healthy container); design/loops.md:36-38 (health observer = manifest probes and Kuma), :84-91 (rollback only on the factory's own ladder); design/model.md:19 (Deployment writer); waves.md:84-86 (health reconciler; restart recipe as the first known error)
objections.test: Replay the #2 and #3 signal streams through W3, with the action executor in dry run and the direct probe/Docker state taken from the recorded truth. Pass: the first planned action on #2 is a config/code fix to the healthcheck (0 restarts), and #3 links 45d7d45 as suspect and plans a config revert of the sync (0 restarts).
objections.proposal: Gate the restart recipe on two independent observations agreeing: Kuma plus a direct probe, Docker state, or evidence of recent successful work such as log lines or DB writes. When they disagree, open `probe.disagrees` on the monitor or healthcheck as subject and route it to the config class. Make monitor and healthcheck syncs (Kuma monitors.yaml, compose healthchecks) emit Deployment events so they attach as suspects. Give config-class rollback a 'revert suspect deployment' action that also covers changes the factory did not ship.

objections.claim: Two things undercut the claim that the 10-17 reboot heals at 0 cost, and both make #9 worse. (1) The candidate gate is frozen at T 30 min / N 1, so every first signal promotes at once. The walk in loops.md has the candidate 'expire as a recovered blip', which cannot happen with N 1. (2) The correlator folds at the host, but known-error matching is per fingerprint: 'container down' maps to the restart recipe. Nothing says that a host-level cause (fresh boot, missing mount, host unreachable) holds the child recipes. During a 7.6-min reboot, restarts race the host coming back. On 10-21 they fail, and '2 failed restarts → escalate to code fix' then spawns code-fix attempts against innocent repos until the per-project breakers trip.
objections.evidence: adr/ADR-003-correlation.md:36-37 (candidate gate T 30 min / N 1); design/loops.md:51-54 (10-17 'expires as a recovered blip'), :69-71 (gate rule), :86 (restart: 2 failures → escalate to code fix), :93-97 (breaker per project and class); waves.md:86 (restart recipe keyed to the 'container down' known error); evidence/incidents/incidents.md:153-160 (boot 20:49-20:56), :250-252 (no shutdown record, drive gone)
objections.test: Replay the 10-17 and 10-21 streams with the recipe executor and planner in dry run. Count planned restarts inside the host's boot window, code-fix Tasks created, and breaker openings. Pass: 0 restarts while a host-level condition is open or within its hold, 0 code-fix Tasks, 0 breakers, and 10-17 ends as a single dismissed or quiet-closed candidate with no investigate spawn.
objections.proposal: Choose the action at the incident level, not per member. When a topology ancestor has an open host condition (boot seen via a wtmp/uptime reconciler, mount, reachability), hold the child recipes for the host's hold window and run the host runbook first. Raise N above 1 for host-folded candidates, or drop N and gate on T plus 'still firing'. Treat a declared reboot (the actor writes intent, as deploys already do) as expected.

objections.claim: The glance heal (gameday row 1) holds only under assumptions the waves don't check. First, the recipe `make -C <project> restart svc=<name>` assumes every infra project has that target, and the manifest drift check doesn't verify it. Second, it treats Docker `stop` as a fault, but the same event comes from a deliberate stop, a RollHook deploy draining replicas (#4's 'overlapping old replicas') and a Watchtower/WUD update, so the reconciler would fight deploys. Third, the ≤ 5 min target rests on a new event recorder, while the daemon's event ring holds under 1 min of history. A recorder outage during the fault loses the edge, and the health reconciler as specified in W3 reads 'signals plus a direct probe', not the container's level state.
objections.evidence: evidence/gameday/2026-10-22-glance.out.md:3-13 (not healed; Kuma +6.8 min); design/proof.md:50-58 ('≤ 5 min holds only with the Docker event recorder'); evidence/signals/signals.md:74 (Docker ring under 1 min on the vps, 1-3 min on the homelab); waves.md:84-87; evidence/incidents/incidents.md:113-117 (deploy churn)
objections.test: Gameday row 1, three variants: (a) `docker stop glance`; (b) a RollHook deploy of a canary service mid-drain; (c) kill the homelab recorder, then `docker stop glance`. Pass: (a) and (c) healed ≤ 5 min (c through a resync level read of `docker ps`), (b) gets 0 restarts, and `factory manifest check` fails on a project whose runtime lacks the restart target.
objections.proposal: Define desired state as the manifest runtime minus any in-flight Deployment or declared maintenance. RollHook, WUD and `make deploy` record intent before they stop anything. Have the health reconciler read container level state (`docker ps` / inspect) on every resync and use events only as a wake-up. Add the restart target to the drift check for every `runtime` entry.

objections.claim: #5 (the MacBook vault-backup heartbeat, missing 108 h) relies on an 'expected-unavailable' class that exists only in incidents.md, not in loops, model or any ADR. Under the spec, the push monitor opens health.down, passes T 30 min, promotes, spawns an investigation with no recipe, and sits open in Argo for 4.5 days. Meanwhile the real risk, a vault backup that didn't run, raises nothing, because a backup has no SLO and so the heads-up tier never fires.
objections.evidence: evidence/incidents/incidents.md:131-144 (and :141, the class named only there); design/loops.md:36-44 (no host-availability notion; `infra.backup` listed only for host projects); adr/ADR-014-owner-decisions.md:26-28
objections.test: Replay e268 (07-04 18:30 → 07-09 06:30) through W3. Count investigate spawns and open incident-hours, and check whether a backup-age condition exists. Pass: 0 investigate spawns, 1 `infra.backup` condition once age passes the policy, closed by the next successful run.
objections.proposal: Add `availability: intermittent` to manifest runtime targets (the MacBook). For those, replace the liveness heartbeat with an age condition on the job's output (`infra.backup` age > policy) and suppress investigation while the host is merely absent.
